items.title: No local weekly series of missed reconciliation items
items.whyItMatters: The August check is one snapshot of 60 handoffs; without weekly baseline points a run chart cannot show whether a later fall is a real shift or ordinary variation.
items.opportunity: Collect eight weekly baseline points of 20 handoff sheets each before the first PDSA cycle.

items.title: Effects fade when feedback stops
items.whyItMatters: The only controlled evaluation lost its effect within seven months once feedback ended (claim c2), so a short project could overstate what the ward keeps.
items.opportunity: Build fortnightly feedback at the huddle into the change and track checklist completion as a process measure.

items.title: Patient harm is not measured in the retrieved evidence
items.whyItMatters: Missed items are a process measure; adverse drug events are too rare on one ward to show a change in three months.
items.opportunity: Report pharmacist-found discrepancies that reached the patient as a descriptive count, without claiming an effect on harm.

items.title: Patients with hearing or cognitive impairment take part far less
items.whyItMatters: Bedside involvement helps patients who can take part and bypasses those who cannot (claim c4), widening differences in who is protected.
items.opportunity: Record whether the patient took part in the bedside medicines check and report missed items separately for patients who could not.

items.title: Reviewer knowledge of the period may bias sheet review
items.whyItMatters: Sheet review finds about four in five missed items (claim c3) but is not blind; a reviewer who expects improvement may code borderline items leniently.
items.opportunity: Use a written operational definition with examples and have the pharmacist double-review a random 10 percent of sheets each fortnight.

errorsFound: The need implies the checklist will prevent harm; the retrieved evidence supports fewer missed items, not fewer adverse drug events.
reevaluation: The gaps point to a measurement-first QI project: establish a weekly baseline, test the checklist in small cycles with fortnightly feedback, report participation by impairment, and keep harm claims out of the aim.
summary: Five gaps: missing baseline series, fading effects without feedback, no harm data, unequal participation, and measurement bias.
